audit_type: Independent mathematical derivation and finite numerical diagnostics
not_a_claim_of: a Lean certificate for these stabilization rules
global convexity or monotonicity of recentered numerical stream values
preservation of the gradients of the original unstabilized convex components

local_identity.assumption: Fplus(p,n)-Fminus(p,n)=f(p-n), with differentiability or explicitly matched selected backward conventions.
local_identity.jacobian: P=[[A,B],[C,D]], J=Df(p-n): A-C=J and B-D=-J, equivalently [I,-I]P=J[I,-I].
local_identity.consequence: Any equal correction to the two output Jacobian rows leaves the signed derivative identity unchanged. Composition preserves the original network derivative when local residuals and backward conventions match.

forward_recentring.formula: C=(Fplus+Fminus)/2, d=f(p-n). Subtract C-|d|/2 from both outputs to obtain dplus,dminus as numerical values.
forward_recentring.stable_evaluation: Evaluate d through the local ordinary primitive, not by subtracting two enormous streams. The separately evaluated full original model remains a validation reference, not a source of substituted activations or gradients.
forward_recentring.scope: Detached correction changes the interpretation of the individual stream sensitivities. They are algorithmic frozen-reference quantities, not gradients of globally convex recentered functions.

backward_shift.common_and_difference: R_alpha scales the cotangent sum by lambda and preserves its difference.
backward_shift.proxy_pullback: The detached common-derivative proxy gives P_transpose R_alpha: an output-adjoint shift before the local pullback.
backward_shift.formal_mlp_schedule: The formal recurrence is s_l=R_alpha_l P_l_transpose s_(l+1), with output source R_alpha_L. The before-pull form is equivalent after moving each shift to the preceding logical block's output boundary and applying the final input-boundary shift. The input-boundary shift does not change unified=(splus-sminus)/2.
backward_shift.grouping_requirement: To match the MLP theorem, count one shift per logical affine-ReLU block boundary. Inserting extra shifts at affine, reshape, transpose, or layout nodes defines a different attribution algorithm.
backward_shift.half_shift_control: alpha=1/2 everywhere yields positive and negative unified head sensitivities equal to plus/minus one half of the original gradient.
backward_shift.seed_independence: Separate head passes must use the same shifts fixed from forward data or parameters. Seed-dependent shift choices can break gradient reconstruction, as the explicit two-by-two counterexample demonstrates.

numerical_basis_recommendation.difference_path: The antisymmetric cotangent evolves by the ordinary primitive VJP. Propagating it explicitly avoids recovering a small model gradient by subtracting enormous head sensitivities.
numerical_basis_recommendation.common_path: The common contribution uses the actual paired primitive VJP evaluated at recentered stream states, with the declared shift schedule.
numerical_basis_recommendation.adaptive_joint_variant: Jointly damping the average of two source-head cotangents preserves their difference by construction, but is a separate algorithm from formal shiftPair unless equivalence is proved. It must not be silently substituted for the MLP shift schedule.

boundary_findings: Initial differentiable positive/negative clamping can give a difference derivative of two or zero at a zero input. A balanced straight-through lift p=x/2+stopgrad(|x|/2), n=-x/2+stopgrad(|x|/2) preserves the unit derivative.
At a ReLU tie, torch.maximum(p,n)-n and torch.relu(p-n) may select different derivatives. An explicit inactive-at-tie gate matches the native ReLU convention tested here.
A fixed common input shift changes the individual product-head gradients, so the ReLU MLP head-Jacobian shift-equivariance argument does not extend unchanged to products.
